conceptZh: 椅：木加奇，木頭做成可以坐的椅子。
object: a tiny felt ninja who is bad at hiding, a mimicking mini ninja twin, and a red toy chair
morph: the twin copies every move a beat late, so the pair collide and mix up chair parts into 椅
creativeAngle: 布忍者和慢一拍的小複製忍者撞在一起，搬椅子零件拼出椅。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 椅 (chair), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a tiny felt ninja who is bad at hiding, a mimicking mini ninja twin, and a red toy chair. Light blue-gray backdrop with a thin wooden floor stripe; the glyph is cherry-red. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: a navy felt ninja tiptoes in, crouches behind a lamp-post-thin pole, and thinks he is invisible; the voice says the first 椅 as a red wooden stroke slides in from the left. 1.5-3.0s: a smaller twin ninja pops up, copying his tiptoe, his crouch, his wave, always one beat late; the voice says the second 椅 as both reach for the same stroke and bonk heads. 3.0-4.5s: they swap sides, tug the pieces the wrong way, then spin and the strokes lock into the red 椅 at 70% of frame height. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 搖椅 (ㄧㄠˊ ㄧˇ) as a little rocking chair swings in and both ninjas hop on, tipping and rocking. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is still; the twins rock gently side by side at the edge, the small one a beat behind. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Voice: one gentle off-screen voice in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, slow with crisp tones, reads precisely 椅、椅、搖椅 = ㄧˇ、ㄧˇ、ㄧㄠˊ ㄧˇ, character, character, word, and nothing after it. Keep any background music quieter than the voice. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 椅 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.

conceptZh: 發條鯊魚只想坐上一張小椅子，卻把發條轉得太緊，衝過頭一口咬進木板堆，木板飛起來落成紅色的「椅」，牠冒煙轉圈後輕輕一跳，終於穩穩坐上椅子。
object: a chunky wind-up toy shark with an oversized tail key, a tiny blue toy chair, and a stack of short wooden planks
morph: the shark overshoots the chair and chomps the plank stack; the planks burst up and rain down, landing as the strokes of 椅 (木 on the left, 奇 on the right), while the chair stays a separate prop at the corner
creativeAngle: 全新「用力過頭」橋段：坐椅子是最簡單的小事，鯊魚卻把發條轉到冒煙，衝過頭撞進木板堆，撞擊把木板震成「椅」的筆畫；配詞「椅子」正好在牠終於坐下那一刻說出，聽到與看到完全同步。不用機器人，不沿用上一版忍者搖椅。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 椅 (chair), correctly formed with 木 on the left and 奇 on the right, in saturated cherry-red against a pale cream background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead: a chunky wind-up toy shark with a big silver tail key, rubbery grey body, goofy wide grin and a habit of chomping at everything. Props: one tiny blue toy chair at bottom right, and a neat stack of short wooden planks at the far right edge. Simple flat floor, nothing busy behind.

0.0-1.5s: the shark enters from the left, stops, and stares hard at the tiny chair. It just wants to sit down. Instead of walking over, it grabs its own tail key and cranks it with enormous effort, tongue out, key clicking faster and faster until the whole body shivers. The voice says the first 椅 as the plank stack wobbles in anticipation.

1.5-3.0s: release. The shark rockets straight across the frame, shoots clean past the chair, and chomps mouth-first into the plank stack. BIG BONK: squash-and-stretch, the stack bursts upward, planks tumbling in the air.

3.0-4.5s: the shark skids backward with smoking feet, then spins in a tight dizzy circle on dry land, eyes going round and round. While it spins, the planks rain down one by one and land exactly as the red strokes of 椅, centered, filling about 70% of frame height. The voice says the second 椅 as the last stroke drops into place.

4.5-5.5s: the shark shakes off the dizziness, looks at the little chair, and this time gives one gentle hop. It plops neatly onto the blue chair at bottom right, tail key still ticking. The voice says 椅子 exactly as it lands on the chair.

5.5-8.0s: final hold. The glyph 椅 stays perfectly still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Away from the strokes, the shark sits proudly on the chair, swinging its tail, then the chair tips back a tiny bit and rocks forward again, and the shark grins.

Voice: one warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwan-standard Mandarin, slow, with crisp distinct tones, reads precisely 椅、椅、椅子 (ㄧˇ、ㄧˇ、ㄧˇ ㄗ˙), character, character, word, and nothing after it. No other dialogue, no English. Any background music stays quieter than the voice. The vocabulary word is audio only: the glyph 椅 is the only text on screen, with no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects. All characters are stylized toys; no real people or realistic human figures. Bright but not neon, no white blowouts, no dark grading.
